title: Sell Mineral Rights in Lindsay, TX
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Lindsay, TX
metaDescription: Lindsay sits in Reeves County, among the most heavily drilled Delaware Basin ground since the horizontal boom took hold around 2016. We buy interests here directly.
heroLead: Reeves County has been one of the busiest counties in the entire Permian since the horizontal drilling push really took off, and Lindsay sits right in that footprint.
intro: If you own minerals near Lindsay, you're in one of the most actively developed corners of the Delaware Basin. Operators have run large multi-well programs across Reeves County for close to a decade now, targeting stacked Wolfcamp and Bone Spring benches.

sections.heading: Why activity here moves valuations quickly
paragraphs: With this much drilling concentrated in one county, permits and completions near your tract can shift what your interest is worth in a matter of months, not years. We check current Railroad Commission filings on offset sections before every offer, since a permit filed last quarter can matter as much as a well already producing.

sections.heading: Multiple benches, multiple units
paragraphs: It's common for Reeves County acreage to be pooled into several separate spacing units targeting different Wolfcamp benches under the same surface tract. We check every unit tied to your interest rather than pricing off whichever well happens to be on your most recent check stub.

sections.heading: What we watch for on Lindsay-area title
paragraphs: Given the pace of development, some tracts near Lindsay have seen multiple lease amendments and division order revisions over just the last few years. We pull the most current recorded documents from the Reeves County Clerk rather than working off anything you were sent when the lease was first signed.

faqs.question: Is Lindsay still seeing active drilling?
faqs.answer: Reeves County has been one of the most actively drilled counties in the Permian for close to a decade, and Lindsay sits within that footprint. We check current permits near your tract before quoting.

faqs.question: Could my acreage be part of more than one spacing unit?
faqs.answer: Yes, that's common in Reeves County given how many Wolfcamp benches get developed separately under the same surface tract. We check all of them before making an offer.

faqs.question: How quickly can values change here?
faqs.answer: Faster than in a lot of other Permian counties given the pace of development. A new permit filed on an offset section can meaningfully change what we'd offer, so we work off current filings, not last year's data.

faqs.question: My division order has been amended more than once. Which version do you use?
faqs.answer: We pull the most recently recorded version from the Reeves County Clerk and confirm it against current operator records rather than relying on whichever copy you happen to have on hand.
